findingDetails.title: The bare-name probe runs a command-chosen opencode<N> binary from PATH before any rule decides
findingDetails.scopeProof: opencode-version.mjs is in the removal commit's own diff (git show ba9720f2f08 --stat, 21 lines) and was read in full; dispatch-rule-checks.mjs:1108 is the only production caller that passes a command-derived name
findingDetails.claim: The version resolver executes a PATH-resolved binary whose name the evaluated command supplied (opencode<N>), while the path-qualified branch refuses to execute a file the command merely names.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the full resolver for a gate on the bare-name branch (none: no realpath identity check, no allowlist); checked the caller can only supply opencode<N> / $OPENCODE_BIN; checked the probe spawns --version with exit 0 required and a 3s timeout; checked the README row describing bare-name probing as intended.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A bare name is operator-controlled because PATH is operator-controlled, so executing it is no worse than executing opencode. Rejected as a full explanation: the name executed is chosen by the dispatch text, and the module comment fixes the intent as must-not-run a file the command merely names; opencode1 and opencode2 are exactly where a command-chosen name and a real installed file coincide.
findingDetails.confidence: high on mechanism, medium on impact
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If no supported install can have an executable named opencode<N> with a non-empty N on PATH, the finding is documentation-only and still P2.
